How Quiz Arena works, in plain English

Long image

A

Answer

One Worker serves the pages and the login. One Durable Object runs the quiz for everybody. Every file has one small job, so the system stays easy to change.

  1. The browser pages live in public/ and load on anydevice.
  2. The Worker checks logins and forwards game messages.
  3. The Durable Object keeps players, answers, timers, rankings and events.
  4. The Display page reads a safe copy of the game for screen sharing.

Applies toCloudflare Workersone quiz room70–80 studentsno camera and no separate database server

1

What does the whole system look like?

Diagram structure
  • Student phone or laptop student
  • Admin laptop on HDMI admin
  • Display screen for the class display
  • Cloudflare Worker worker
  • Durable Object quiz room room
  • GitHub repository github
  • student → worker · join, answer, rejoin
  • admin → worker · login, start, allow
  • display → worker · safe live view
  • worker → room · state and messages
  • github → worker · deploy code

The Worker is the front door. It never runs on a student device. The Durable Object is the single room that keeps everyone in step.

3

What is the tech stack?

LayerChoiceWhy it fits
PagesHTML, CSS, plain JavaScriptNo build step and easy edits
Edge serverCloudflare WorkerRuns near students with HTTPS
Real timeWebSocket through a Durable ObjectOne room keeps everyone in step
StorageDurable Object storageQuestions, answers, feedback, events
LoginPBKDF2 hash and signed cookieNo plain password in the repo
DeploymentWrangler CLIOne command to publish
SourceGitHubCode history and tests

No Node server stays awake. No SQL database is needed for a class session.

4

What does the backend do exactly?

Diagram structure
  • Teacher signs in login
  • Admin starts a question start
  • Question reaches every device send
  • Student submits an answer answer
  • Room grades and stores it grade
  • Ranking reaches every screen rank
  • Next question starts next
  • answer → grade · via Worker
  • grade → rank · all answered or timer ends
  • login → start · session accepted
  • rank → next · after five seconds
  • send → answer · student taps
  • start → send · broadcast
  1. Sign in ↗

    The Worker checks the hash and sets a signed cookie.

  2. Start ↗

    The room clears old answers and starts the timer.

  3. Answer ↗

    The room grades MCQs by option and text by keywords.

  4. Rank ↗

    The room sends rank, name, roll number and points.

  5. Continue ↗

    The room starts the next question by itself.

5

How does one answer travel?

Diagram structure
  • Student page browser
  • Worker worker
  • Durable Object room
  • Admin page admin
  • Display page display
  • browser → worker · WebSocket answer
  • worker → room · forward answer to grade and store
  • room → browser · answer locked
  • room → admin · Thinking becomes Answered
  • room → display · activity event
  • room → browser · ranking at round end

The Worker never decides who is correct. The room does that once, then tells each screen what that screen may show.

7

What should you remember on class day?

Keep these in mind

- Keep the Admin tab open. It holds the teacher session and the room alive. - Share the Display link when projecting. It hides answers and controls. - Tell students to keep the quiz tab open. Switching apps signs them out. - Five or more waiting students are allowed back automatically. - Download feedback from the Admin button and send that CSV to the developer.
